chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them) narrated:

He said: The believer moves about in five [aspects] of light: his entry is light, his exit is light, his knowledge is light, his speech is light, and his appearance on the Day of Resurrection is towards the light.
ai.seo_question: What are the five aspects of light in a believer's life according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) utilizes the metaphor of 'rolling in light' to signify the comprehensive spiritual purity of a believer, encompassing their origin, demise, intellect, and speech. It reflects the Shia theological concept of *Nur* as both an inner divine illumination and an outward manifestation of faith, culminating in the radiant countenance described in the Quranic eschatology.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 5-20 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn al-Muqayrih, on the authority of A-Muqayrih, on the authority of Talha ibn Zayd, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB), on the authority of his forefathers (MGB) that Ali (MGB) said, “

A believer rolls in five types of light: There is light from where he comes; there is light from where he leaves; there is light in his knowledge; there is light in his speech and there is light in him on the Resurrection Day.”
